extracted.intended_audience: Canadian farmers, horticulturists, home canners, and rural readers seeking practical agricultural/packing guidance
extracted.subtask_description: Practical how-to and regulatory guidance for agricultural tasks (propagating cuttings, planting shelter belts, selecting poultry breeders) and for food/egg packing (candling, canned fruit packing) aimed at farmers and packers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Green candling light as standard for egg candling
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of a green glass filter for egg candling has been evolved from research and is gaining popularity; many commercial firms and departmental officers are using green light exclusively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research indicates blue would be ideal (it lacks yolk color) but the human eye is not very sensitive to blue for practical candling purposes; therefore a green glass filter is recommended and increasingly adopted for standardizing candling equipment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wholesome canned fruit: packing and quality requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: All fruit for cold pack must be sound, wholesome, and fit for human food; fruit must be well washed in clear water; barrels, cans, etc., must be clean and thoroughly sterilized before filling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Packers must grade fruit for quality consistent with established grades for the same variety used for canning. Packers of cord-pack fruit are required to keep daily records of the total weight of fruit and sugar used. (Ensure sanitary containers, proper washing, grading to standard, and record-keeping.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Sketch requirements for shelter-belt/tree-planting assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must send a sketch showing the full length and breadth of the land prepared for planting the shelter belt, the distance between the inside of the proposed belt and any permanent buildings, and the position of any existing plantations or belts of trees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measurements should be given in yards (not rods or feet). Include positions of permanent buildings relative to the proposed belt and any existing plantations so the Forest Service can accurately calculate the number of trees required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best practices for propagating trees by cuttings
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain western trees (willows, Russian poplars, cottonwood, balsam poplar) are easily propagated by cuttings provided several conditions are observed: cuttings must never be allowed to dry out; never pushed into soil without first making a hole; the cutting itself must contain plenty of moisture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Soil must be consistently moist and in close contact with the entire buried portion of the cutting; tramp soil firmly down to avoid pockets around the lower part. Plant cuttings on a slant (buds upward) rather than upright. Do not allow more than one to one-and-a-half inches to project above ground. If cuttings arrive, keep moist or bury in moist soil until planted; soaking cuttings before planting is recommended. Most failures come from too shallow planting or allowing cuttings to dry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selecting poultry breeding stock—judge by progeny, not appearance
rubrics_metrics.description: A good breeder is judged not by its appearance or current laying, but by the kind of stock (progeny) it produces; the acid test of a good breeder is found in the progeny produced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rely on external inspection (looks or handling) to pick good breeders; focus on the performance of offspring from a mating to determine breeder quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Units and measurement conventions for planting/forestry applications
rubrics_metrics.description: When providing measurements for planting or shelter belts, use yards as the unit and ensure full dimensions (length and breadth) are supplied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid giving measurements in rods or feet; using yards standardizes inputs for Forest Service calculations and reduces errors in tree quantity estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pattern ordering instructions (consumer sewing patterns)
rubrics_metrics.description: When ordering a sewing pattern, provide the pattern number and size, your name and address, and include payment (20 cents) in stamps or coin (coin preferred and to be wrapped carefully).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify size (examples given: 14, 16, 18 years, 36, 38, 40 inches bust), note yardage required for sizes (e.g., size 16 requires 1 5/8 yards of 39-inch material), and address the order to the supplier (e.g., Winnipeg Newspaper Un., 175 McDermot Ave., Winnipeg).
